What is real here and what is not

  • Joybot is drawn from his real sprite sheets. Pulling uses your nine new back-to-camera frames, lined up by machine the way you do it by eye (slid until the overlap is blackest; they moved 6 pixels at most), in the order you drew them. Carrying uses the nervous oops. The slap is discarding-clip, and he salutes before flying home.
  • Whatever he grabs is pinned to his fists, frame by frame: the seam, the peeling corner, the bed sheet and the wipe edge. What he carries sits in his fists at his chest, with his mouth showing over it.
  • While he waits for your answer he does his hover from the chat: the same slow figure eight with gentle leans, using the chat's own numbers.
  • The star field is my sketch of VisLab's Lyric Flight. On the phone it will be the real one, recoloured from the leaving room's gradient to the arriving room's.
  • The two rooms are sketches of JoyBrush and Studio, not screenshots. On the phone the show uses pictures of your real screens.
  • The motion is a fair guide. The speed is not: nothing here has been measured on the Note 9.
  • The colours are the app's own: JoyBrush's purple to blue, Studio's mint to lime. On this page the new room comes in from the left. In the app it comes in from the RIGHT: on the lobby dial Studio is the next room to the right of JoyBrush (found on the phone, 16 Nov), so every move is played mirrored there.
